A tag that is itself shared escalates to the whole session id,\n   because a disambiguator that settles nothing looks like it settled something. */\nexport function disambiguate(entries) {\n  const list = entries || [];\n  const counts = new Map();\n  for (const entry of list) {\n    counts.set(entry.identity.base, (counts.get(entry.identity.base) || 0) + 1);\n  }\n\n  const escalated = new Set();\n  const tagsByBase = new Map();\n  for (const entry of list) {\n    if ((counts.get(entry.identity.base) || 0) < 2) continue;\n    const tags = tagsByBase.get(entry.identity.base) || new Map();\n    const tag = sessionTag(entry.sourceSessionId);\n    tags.set(tag, (tags.get(tag) || 0) + 1);\n    tagsByBase.set(entry.identity.base, tags);\n  }\n  for (const [base, tags] of tagsByBase) {\n    for (const [tag, count] of tags) if (count > 1) escalated.add(base + \" \" + tag);\n  }\n\n  return list.map((entry) => {\n    const identity = entry.identity;\n    if ((counts.get(identity.base) || 0) < 2) return identity;\n    const tag = sessionTag(entry.sourceSessionId);\n    const unique = escalated.has(identity.base + \" \" + tag)\n      ? String(entry.sourceSessionId || \"\").trim()\n      : tag;\n    /* Nothing stable to separate them by. A tag derived from position would\n       change between refreshes, which is the bug this module exists to remove,\n       so the duplicate stays visible rather than being papered over. */\n    if (!unique) return identity;\n    return Object.assign({}, identity, {\n      name: identity.base + \" #\" + unique,\n      disambiguator: unique,\n    });\n  });\n}\n\n/* Attention, in one place — the discrete, actionable half of the console.\n\n   The header is CONFIDENCE: continuous, measured quantities about the fleet,\n   each carrying its own provenance, answering \"can I trust this board, and what\n   is this costing me\". This is ATTENTION: discrete items, each carrying kind,\n   severity, exact source, lifecycle, plain-English evidence, impact and a route,\n   answering \"what needs me, and why\".\n\n   The seam is one line: the header never links, and this never aggregates.\n   Everything here is an ITEM — one thing, one source, one route — because a\n   count of to-dos rendered as a metric is the defect this surface exists to\n   remove.\n\n   Pure derivation, no DOM, so the model and its renderer are testable apart the\n   way pulseStripModel already splits them.\n\n   It imports leaf modules only. app.js is the entry point and exports almost\n   nothing, so the two resolvers that genuinely live there arrive as injected\n   functions rather than being re-derived here — the shape notificationPlan\n   already uses for `nameFor`, and for the same reason: a second derivation of\n   one quantity is how two surfaces come to disagree about it. */\n\n/* isTerminal, deliberately NOT isLive.\n\n   \"Still has current impact\" is \"this session has not ended\", and isLive is\n   narrower than that: it excludes `unverified`, a session the board can watch\n   but cannot confirm. Demoting a finding because the sessions it names are\n   unverified would bury exactly the rows the board is least sure about — and\n   styles.css already carries the scar of that conflation (\"Sharing --ended's\n   clay is what made an unverifiable session LOOK finished before it was called\n   finished\"). Unverified is its own state, and it is not an ending. */\nimport { declaredQuiet, isTerminal } from \"./agent-model.js\";\nimport { fmtElapsed } from \"./text-formatters.js\";\nimport {\n  agentName,\n  agentsById,\n  conciseText,\n  investigationView,\n  issueLifecycle,\n  issuesOf,\n  snapshotAgents,\n} from \"./presentation.js\";\n\n/* The blocking/noticed partition, named.\n\n   S0-T2 puts `attentionClass` on the wire beside `attentionSignal`. It is\n   be-dwell's and it is not shipping yet — but the partition is not new\n   detection, it is a NAME for a split the server's attention detectors already\n   compute one kind at a time. So this reads the server's word when there is\n   one and otherwise applies S0-T2's rule to the `attentionSignal.kind` that is\n   on the wire today.\n\n   Server wins on the classification. That is the bandContextPct shape — the\n   server's number, a client walk only as the fallback — and it is here for the\n   same reason: one quantity must not have two answers.\n\n   Without the fallback there is no handoff feed at all until be-dwell lands,\n   and the whole point of shipping this before the header stops linking is that\n   no window exists where a finding is unreachable. */\nconst BLOCKING_KINDS = new Set([\n  \"permission-requested\",\n  \"input-requested\",\n  \"fork-unresolved\",\n  \"handoff-stated\",\n  \"question-pending\",\n  \"assumption-stated\",\n]);\n\nconst NOTICED_KINDS = new Set([\"stalled-active\"]);\n\n/* `nothing-wanted`, `out-of-scope` and `not-readable` deliberately have no\n   class. Absence, not a third value: \"we looked and nothing wants you\", \"it is\n   finished\" and \"there was nothing to read\" are three different facts and none\n   of them is an item. */\n\nexport function attentionClassOf(agent) {\n  if (!agent) return null;\n  /* The stand-down is a VETO both sides compute from the same two fields, not a\n     second opinion about the classification. It runs on the server's word as\n     well as on the derived one — applied to both, the two can never disagree;\n     applied to one, a server that forgot would re-alert a lane the operator\n     explicitly stood down. The atlas-hardening T6/T7 precedence is read here,\n     never reopened: a `parked`/`done` declaration yields no class, and the one\n     thing that reopens it is a needsInput hook strictly newer than the\n     declaration, which declaredQuiet already tests. */\n  if (declaredQuiet(agent)) return null;\n  const declared = agent.attentionClass;\n  if (declared === \"blocking\" || declared === \"noticed\") return declared;\n  const kind = agent.attentionSignal && agent.attentionSignal.kind;\n  if (BLOCKING_KINDS.has(kind)) return \"blocking\";\n  if (NOTICED_KINDS.has(kind)) return \"noticed\";\n  return null;\n}\n\n/* Item ids ARE the board's ids.\n\n   A handoff item for an agent is `agent:<id>` — the exact id issuesOf mints for\n   that same agent. So the S1 parity gate is an identity check rather than a\n   mapping table, and the dedup between the two feeds falls out of a Set. */\nconst agentItemId = (agentId) => \"agent:\" + agentId;\n\nconst defaultProgramName = (program) => (program ? program.name || \"\" : \"\");\n\n/* The honest degradation when app.js has not injected issueImpactLine: say what\n   the server said, or say nothing rather than invent a consequence. */\nconst defaultImpact = (issue) =>\n  (issue && typeof issue.impactSummary === \"string\" && issue.impactSummary.trim()) || \"\";\n\n/* Evidence is the sentence the operator reads INSTEAD of opening the drawer, so\n   it is bounded but never cut mid-word — conciseText is the client's one\n   existing answer to that. The limit is the mockup's peek line at 452px, which\n   wraps to two lines and no more. */\nconst EVIDENCE_LIMIT = 168;\n\n/* A timestamp is only a duration if it is behind the clock.\n\n   `since` drives the per-row wait (\"1h 04m\") and the standby hero. A server\n   instant that is AHEAD of this browser is clock skew, not a negative wait, and\n   liveElapsedText already carries the scar of that drift. Unmeasurable is null:\n   the renderer withholds the reading rather than printing 0m, which is the\n   S0-T1 rule — absent when unmeasurable, never `updatedAt`, never 0. */\nfunction measuredSince(iso, now) {\n  if (typeof iso !== \"string\" || !iso) return null;\n  const ms = Date.parse(iso);\n  if (!Number.isFinite(ms)) return null;\n  return ms > now ? null : iso;\n}\n\n/* severity \"blocking\" means A PERSON IS THE BLOCKER, and nothing else earns it\n   — not a failed collector, not an error-severity system fault.\n\n   That is not a softening of how bad those are. It is what makes the badge\n   contract structural instead of a second rule the badge has to remember: ember\n   is filled exactly when some item is severity \"blocking\", so if the button is\n   red, someone stopped and is waiting for you. Urgency that is not a person\n   lives in `kind` and in the evidence sentence. */\nfunction handoffItem(agent, program, attentionClass, now, programNameFor) {\n  const blocking = attentionClass === \"blocking\";\n  const name = agentName(agent);\n  const inProgram = programNameFor(program);\n  const signal = agent.attentionSignal || {};\n  return {\n    id: agentItemId(agent.id),\n    kind: \"handoff\",\n    severity: blocking ? \"blocking\" : \"warning\",\n    source: {\n      agentId: agent.id,\n      agentName: name,\n      programId: agent.programId || (program && program.id) || \"\",\n      programName: inProgram,\n    },\n    lifecycle: agent.hookLifecycle || \"unknown\",\n    evidence: conciseText(signal.evidence || agent.statusReason || \"\", EVIDENCE_LIMIT),\n    impact: blocking\n      ? `${name} is stopped and cannot continue until you answer.`\n      : `${name} has gone quiet. Nothing is waiting on you; the watcher is reporting it.`,\n    /* PERMANENTLY NULL, and that is a ruling rather than a gap.\n\n       docs/S0-T1-DEAD-TIME-MEASUREMENT.md measured every candidate for \"when\n       did this person-block begin\" and none of them is an entry edge:\n       `hookLifecycleAt` advanced 01:38:51 → 01:39:16 → 01:40:41 on a session\n       that stayed needsInput throughout, so it is a write clock; the hook\n       Notification repeats mid-wait, so it would RESET the age during a single\n       block; Stop and UserPromptSubmit mark turn and return boundaries, not\n       entry; and the cmux journal rolls away, so it is not durable history.\n\n       So dead time is dropped, not deferred. The one thing this field may never\n       become is a heartbeat, because a heartbeat here makes the oldest wait on\n       the board read as the newest — which is worse than showing no age at all.\n       An item's own age still exists where it is genuinely measured: a finding\n       has an openedAt and an investigation has a createdAt, and both are\n       durable server facts about a record rather than guesses about a person. */\n    since: null,\n    route: { kind: \"agent\", id: agent.id },\n  };\n}\n\n/* The one line with a FACT in it.\n\n   A degraded-source issue arrives carrying three layers of category and one\n   layer of evidence, and until now the item took a category:\n\n     title             \"Cursor collection is degraded\"\n     summary           \"1 collection problem makes Cursor session data\n                        potentially incomplete.\"\n     technicalDetails  [\"cursor GUI conversations: unable to open database file\"]\n\n   Only the third says what is wrong. §4.2 requires evidence to be a plain-English\n   whole sentence, and shipping the summary here put a category where the evidence\n   belongs — so the operator read \"Whoops\" three times and never once learned that\n   a database would not open. technicalDetails rendered only in the drawer, three\n   clicks from the chip that was complaining.\n\n   Read off the FIELD, not off today's wording: the collectors are being taught to\n   phrase these as whole sentences naming the population they lost, and this picks\n   that up for free when it lands. Multiple faults join rather than truncate to the\n   first, because \"which one\" is exactly what a count already failed to say.\n\n   Falls back to the summary when a source ships no detail — a category is a poor\n   evidence line but an empty one is worse. */\nfunction faultEvidence(issue) {\n  const details = Array.isArray(issue.technicalDetails) ? issue.technicalDetails : [];\n  const said = details.filter((d) => typeof d === \"string\" && d.trim()).map((d) => d.trim());\n  return said.join(\" · \") || issue.summary || issue.title || \"\";\n}\n\nfunction dataflowItem(issue, snap, now, programNameFor, impactFor) {\n  const life = issueLifecycle(issue);\n  const affected = (issue.affectedAgentIds || []).map((id) => agentsById(snap).get(id)).filter(Boolean);\n  const one = affected.length === 1 ? affected[0] : null;\n  return {\n    id: issue.id,\n    kind: \"dataflow\",\n    severity: \"warning\",\n    source: one\n      ? {\n        agentId: one.agent.id,\n        agentName: agentName(one.agent),\n        programId: one.agent.programId || (one.program && one.program.id) || \"\",\n        programName: programNameFor(one.program),\n      }\n      : { collector: issue.kind === \"system\" ? \"control-plane\" : \"\" },\n    lifecycle: life.state,\n    evidence: conciseText(faultEvidence(issue), EVIDENCE_LIMIT),\n    /* The pairing the raw string needs. `impact` names WHICH sessions the fault\n       costs the operator and `since` names WHEN it started, so the fault sentence\n       never stands alone as a library error with no consequence attached. */\n    impact: impactFor(issue, snap),\n    since: measuredSince(life.verificationStartedAt || life.openedAt, now),\n    /* The same severity→drawer split findingFromIssue already uses, so an item\n       and the strip finding it replaces open the same panel. */\n    route: { kind: issue.severity === \"error\" ? \"intervention\" : \"advisory\", id: issue.id },\n  };\n}\n\nfunction investigationItem(item, now) {\n  const view = investigationView(item.state);\n  const agents = Number.isFinite(item.affectedAgents) ? item.affectedAgents : null;\n  const programs = Number.isFinite(item.affectedPrograms) ? item.affectedPrograms : null;\n  return {\n    id: item.issueId,\n    kind: \"investigation\",\n    severity: \"warning\",\n    source: { collector: item.runModel || \"\" },\n    lifecycle: view.work,\n    evidence: conciseText(item.rationale || item.headline || \"\", EVIDENCE_LIMIT),\n    impact: agents != null && programs != null\n      ? `Covers ${agents} session${agents === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"} across ${programs} program${programs === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"}. It runs without you.`\n      : \"It runs without you; nothing here is waiting.\",\n    since: measuredSince(item.startedAt || item.createdAt, now),\n    route: { kind: \"investigation\", id: item.issueId },\n  };\n}\n\n/* The promotion predicate — the ONE gate between live and history.\n\n   Every row of the truth table resolves its evidence through the item's own\n   route, the same way resolveSelection does, so the predicate needs nothing but\n   (item, snap) and can never read a field the drawer would not find. */\nexport function hasCurrentImpact(item, snap) {\n  if (!item || !item.route) return false;\n\n  if (item.route.kind === \"agent\") {\n    const found = agentsById(snap).get(item.route.id);\n    if (!found || isTerminal(found.agent)) return false;\n    /* A person is the blocker, and nothing below outranks it.\n       RE-DERIVED from the snapshot rather than read off item.severity: the\n       predicate is handed a snap precisely so a row built on an earlier paint\n       is judged against the current one. An agent that has since answered, or\n       been stood down, is not still blocking anybody — trusting the item's own\n       frozen severity would pin the first ember it ever earned. */\n    return attentionClassOf(found.agent) !== null;\n  }\n\n  if (item.route.kind === \"investigation\") {\n    /* A queue row's liveness IS its existence — it was built from state.queueItems\n       this paint. Investigations carry no affected-agent set to go stale, and\n       none of their four states is a clearance. */\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  const issue = issuesOf(snap).find((i) => i.id === item.route.id);\n  /* Source healthy / verified: the finding is gone from the current issues, so\n     whatever produced it has cleared. Audit, not attention. */\n  if (!issue) return false;\n  const life = issueLifecycle(issue);\n  if (life.state === \"resolved\") return false;\n\n  const ids = issue.affectedAgentIds || [];\n  const index = agentsById(snap);\n  const liveAffected = ids.filter((id) => {\n    const found = index.get(id);\n    return Boolean(found) && !isTerminal(found.agent);\n  }).length;\n\n  /* Verifying is the WEAKER claim — \"waiting for a fresh source snapshot to\n     clear this\" — so it has to point at something live to stay on the surface.\n     A system-wide finding in verifying has nothing for the operator to do and\n     belongs in history, which is why this row reads the count and not the\n     has-any-ids test the row below it uses. */\n  if (life.state === \"verifying\") return liveAffected > 0;\n\n  /* Stale-without-current-impact. An EMPTY affected list is not stale — it is\n     the system-wide case (\"not tied to a specific agent\"), which is exactly the\n     dataflow fault this surface exists to carry. Only a finding that named\n     agents and whose agents are all gone has lost its impact.\n\n     \"All gone\" has to mean the board CAN SEE them and they have ended — not that\n     it cannot see them at all. Measured on a board with a broken Cursor\n     collector: the issue named 91 sessions, every one absent from the snapshot\n     BECAUSE the collector that would have enumerated them had failed. That made\n     liveAffected 0, and the one item explaining the gap was filed to history by\n     the gap itself. The operator was left with a chip reading \"Readings\n     degraded\" and a panel with nothing in it.\n\n     So the test is agents the index KNOWS. A finding whose named agents are\n     present and terminal has genuinely outlived its subject — the abandoned\n     worktree advisory, the archived session — and is stale. A finding none of\n     whose agents the board can resolve has not outlived anything; it has lost\n     sight of the population, which for a source fault IS the impact. That is\n     the same reasoning the empty-list case above already applies, reached from\n     the other side: an unresolvable list is no more a stale list than an empty\n     one. A source that recovers leaves issuesOf and is cleared above. */\n  const knownAffected = ids.filter((id) => index.has(id)).length;\n  if (ids.length > 0 && liveAffected === 0 && knownAffected > 0) return false;\n  return true;\n}\n\n/* Why an item was demoted, in the words the parity table posts. */\nfunction demotionReason(item, snap) {\n  if (item.route.kind === \"agent\") {\n    const found = agentsById(snap).get(item.route.id);\n    if (!found) return \"agent left the snapshot\";\n    if (isTerminal(found.agent)) return \"session ended\";\n    return \"no longer asking\";\n  }\n  if (item.route.kind === \"investigation\") return \"queue row cleared\";\n  const issue = issuesOf(snap).find((i) => i.id === item.route.id);\n  if (!issue) return \"source healthy — finding cleared\";\n  const life = issueLifecycle(issue);\n  if (life.state === \"resolved\") return \"resolved\";\n  if (life.state === \"verifying\") return \"verifying with no live affected agent\";\n  return \"stale — no live affected agent\";\n}\n\n/* Oldest wait first: the row that has been stopped longest is the one that has\n   cost the most, and an unmeasurable wait sorts last rather than first, because\n   \"we cannot say\" must not outrank a measured hour. Ties break on id so a paint\n   is stable across snapshots. */\nfunction byWaitThenId(a, b) {\n  if (a.since && b.since && a.since !== b.since) return a.since < b.since ? -1 : 1;\n  if (a.since && !b.since) return -1;\n  if (!a.since && b.since) return 1;\n  return a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0;\n}\n\nconst SEVERITY_RANK = { blocking: 0, warning: 1 };\nconst KIND_RANK = { handoff: 0, dataflow: 1, investigation: 2 };\n\nfunction feedOrder(a, b) {\n  const bySeverity = SEVERITY_RANK[a.severity] - SEVERITY_RANK[b.severity];\n  if (bySeverity) return bySeverity;\n  const byKind = KIND_RANK[a.kind] - KIND_RANK[b.kind];\n  if (byKind) return byKind;\n  return byWaitThenId(a, b);\n}\n\n/* Every candidate the three feeds produce, split by the one gate.\n\n   The S1 acceptance gate has to account for every id in issuesOf(snap) ∪\n   queueItems — each resolves to a live item or to a DOCUMENTED demotion — so the\n   demotions cannot be dropped on the floor inside the filter. This is also what\n   S5-T1's History route will read. */\nexport function notificationCandidates(snap, queueItems = [], now = Date.now(), deps = {}) {\n  const programNameFor = deps.programNameFor || defaultProgramName;\n  const impactFor = deps.impactFor || defaultImpact;\n  const candidates = [];\n  const taken = new Set();\n\n  /* handoff — agents the attention layer has classified. Built FIRST so that an\n     agent's `agent:<id>` finding resolves to its own row in its own drawer\n     rather than to an advisory panel about it. */\n  for (const { agent, program } of snapshotAgents(snap)) {\n    const attentionClass = attentionClassOf(agent);\n    if (!attentionClass) continue;\n    const item = handoffItem(agent, program, attentionClass, now, programNameFor);\n    candidates.push(item);\n    taken.add(item.id);\n  }\n\n  /* dataflow — issuesOf, and only issuesOf.\n     §4.2 reads \"issuesOf(snap) + controlHealth.errors/staleSources\", and the\n     second half is already satisfied inside issuesOf, which synthesizes\n     `system:collector-errors` from controlHealth.errors when the server ships no\n     issues array. Going further and minting a client-side id for each error\n     would put rows on this surface that route to a drawer resolveSelection\n     cannot find — issuesOf carries that rule in its own comment, and it was\n     written after seven un-actionable rows shipped to the live board. */\n  for (const issue of issuesOf(snap)) {\n    if (taken.has(issue.id)) continue;\n    const item = dataflowItem(issue, snap, now, programNameFor, impactFor);\n    candidates.push(item);\n    taken.add(item.id);\n  }\n\n  /* investigation — the queue rows whose finding is not already on the list.\n     Same rule pulseFindings uses: when the issue is present it carries the\n     investigation in its own lifecycle, and two rows for one thing is how a\n     list of discrete items starts aggregating. */\n  for (const queued of Array.isArray(queueItems) ? queueItems : []) {\n    if (!queued || taken.has(queued.issueId)) continue;\n    const item = investigationItem(queued, now);\n    candidates.push(item);\n    taken.add(item.id);\n  }\n\n  const live = [];\n  const demoted = [];\n  for (const item of candidates) {\n    if (hasCurrentImpact(item, snap)) live.push(item);\n    else demoted.push({ id: item.id, item, reason: demotionReason(item, snap) });\n  }\n  live.sort(feedOrder);\n  return { live, demoted };\n}\n\nexport function notificationFeed(snap, queueItems = [], now = Date.now(), deps = {}) {\n  return notificationCandidates(snap, queueItems, now, deps).live;\n}\n\n/* The badge's verdict, from the feed rather than from a parallel count.\n\n   `blocked` is exactly \"some item is severity blocking\", which is exactly \"a\n   person is the blocker\" — one derivation, so the ember on the button and the\n   ember rail on the row can never disagree about whether anyone is waiting. */\nexport function feedTone(items) {\n  const list = Array.isArray(items) ? items : [];\n  if (list.some((item) => item.severity === \"blocking\")) return \"blocked\";\n  return list.length ? \"noticed\" : \"clear\";\n}\n\n/* The count the button carries: agents waiting on a PERSON.\n\n   Not the length of the feed. A badge that counted every watched thing would\n   read 9 on a board where nobody is blocked, and the number beside an ember\n   button has to mean the same thing the ember means. */\nexport function blockingCount(items) {\n  return (Array.isArray(items) ? items : []).filter((item) => item.severity === \"blocking\").length;\n}\n\n/* ---------- the panel's model ----------\n\n   Split from the renderer the way pulseStripModel is, so the three sections,\n   the verdict and the withheld hero are all assertable without a DOM. */\n\nconst VERDICT = { blocked: \"Waiting on you\", noticed: \"Watch\", clear: \"All clear\" };\n\n/* The standby hero the rev-2 mockup put in the largest type on this panel is\n   GONE, and no reading replaces it.\n\n   It was the one number here with no measurable source. S0-T1 tried every\n   candidate for the instant a person-block begins and found a write clock, a\n   notification that repeats mid-wait, two boundaries that mark something else,\n   and a journal that rolls away — so the sum of dead time across the fleet\n   cannot be computed at all, and `pulse.standbyMs` is not shipping.\n\n   Deliberately not replaced by a withheld-with-a-reason slot either. That was\n   the right treatment while the field was merely unmeasured; once the answer is\n   \"this quantity is not obtainable from these sources\", a permanent apology in\n   the hero position is furniture. The count leads instead — a count is honest\n   when a duration is not, and it is already the lede. */\n\n/* Program groups, in the order their longest wait started. The feed is already\n   sorted oldest-first, so first-seen order IS that order and no second sort can\n   disagree with the list it groups. */\nfunction groupByProgram(items) {\n  const groups = [];\n  const index = new Map();\n  for (const item of items) {\n    const key = item.source.programId || item.source.programName || \"\";\n    let group = index.get(key);\n    if (!group) {\n      group = { programId: item.source.programId || \"\", programName: item.source.programName || \"Unassigned\", items: [] };\n      index.set(key, group);\n      groups.push(group);\n    }\n    group.items.push(item);\n  }\n  return groups;\n}\n\n/* A notification surface is judged on the day it has nothing to say, so All\n   clear does not go blank — it shows what the watcher is watching. \"Watching,\n   found nothing\" and \"not watching\" are the two states an empty panel is\n   otherwise ambiguous between, and only one of them is good news. */\nfunction proofOfWatch(snap, now) {\n  if (!snap) return null;\n  const working = snap.totals && Number.isFinite(snap.totals.working) ? snap.totals.working : null;\n  const programs = Array.isArray(snap.programs) ? snap.programs.length : null;\n  const scannedMs = Date.parse(snap.generatedAt);\n  return {\n    working,\n    programs,\n    scanAgo: Number.isFinite(scannedMs) && now >= scannedMs ? fmtElapsed(now - scannedMs) : null,\n  };\n}\n\n/* A surface that lists things has to say when its list is short.\n\n   The Findings card used to carry this: an unreachable triage queue made its\n   sublabel read \"Triage queue unavailable (…) — findings may be missing\", which\n   was the one place the operator learned the count below it was a floor rather\n   than a total. That card is retired, and the disclosure cannot retire with it —\n   the strip still refuses to go calm on a queue error, so without this the board\n   would apologise and never say what for.\n\n   It belongs here rather than in the header for the same reason the findings\n   did: it is a fact about THIS list. And unlike a collector fault it needs no\n   minted id, because it is not a finding to open — it is this panel admitting\n   that investigations it would otherwise show are missing. */\nexport function notificationPanelModel(snap, queueItems = [], now = Date.now(), deps = {}) {\n  const { live, demoted } = notificationCandidates(snap, queueItems, now, deps);\n  const blocking = live.filter((item) => item.severity === \"blocking\");\n  const investigations = live.filter((item) => item.kind === \"investigation\");\n  const watching = live.filter((item) => item.severity !== \"blocking\" && item.kind !== \"investigation\");\n  const tone = feedTone(live);\n  return {\n    tone,\n    /* The eyebrow speaks in calmVerdict's words, but it counts what THIS PANEL\n       lists rather than what the board is watching generally. A \"Watch\" over an\n       empty panel — the board eyeing a context peak the center has no item for —\n       would be the surface describing something it does not show. */\n    verdict: VERDICT[tone],\n    count: blocking.length,\n    lede: blocking.length\n      ? `${blocking.length} agent${blocking.length === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"} stopped`\n      : \"Nothing is stopped\",\n    rest: [\n      watching.length ? `${watching.length} quiet` : \"\",\n      investigations.length ? `${investigations.length} running below` : \"\",\n    ].filter(Boolean).join(\" · \"),\n    groups: groupByProgram(blocking),\n    watching,\n    investigations,\n    incomplete: deps.queueError\n      ? `Triage queue unavailable (${deps.queueError}) — investigations may be missing from this list.`\n      : \"\",\n    /* The all-clear proof is withheld while the list is admittedly short. \"41\n       agents working, nothing stopped\" is a claim about the whole board, and it\n       cannot be made from a population we know has a hole in it. */\n    proof: live.length || deps.queueError ? null : proofOfWatch(snap, now),\n    demoted,\n  };\n}\n\n/* The agents delivery is allowed to interrupt someone for.\n\n   Deliberately NARROWER than alerting(), which needsHumanIds read until S1-T5\n   repointed it: alerting is true for any non-healthy non-terminal row, a strict\n   superset of \"a person is the blocker\". Left alone, an out-of-page\n   notification fired for a stalled advisory while the button correctly stayed\n   amber — and the ember contract broke at the one moment the operator cannot\n   see the screen to check it. */\nexport function blockingAgentIds(snap) {\n  const ids = [];\n  for (const { agent } of snapshotAgents(snap)) {\n    if (attentionClassOf(agent) === \"blocking\") ids.push(agent.id);\n  }\n  return ids.sort();\n}\n\n/* Out-of-page alerts — the only part of the console that can interrupt someone\n   who is not looking at it.\n\n   That is why it is its own module. Everything else in the client competes for\n   attention on a screen the operator chose to open; this competes with whatever\n   they are doing instead. The rules that keep that honest are all here and\n   nowhere else: permission is requested from a click and never on load, a\n   notification fires only for agents that newly need a human (never for the\n   standing set, or a reload would re-alert the whole board), and the tab title\n   carries the count so a muted browser still tells the truth.\n\n   Reads `state.notify` and `state.snap`; builds DOM only for its own toggle\n   button. It calls nothing else in the client, which is what let it come out\n   whole. */\n\nimport { $, el } from \"./dom-primitives.js\";\nimport { state } from \"./client-state.js\";\nimport { agentName, agentsById } from \"./presentation.js\";\nimport { blockingAgentIds } from \"./notification-center.js\";\n\nexport const NOTIFY_STORAGE_KEY = \"mtn3-notify\";\n\nexport const NOTIFY_TAG = \"anthill-needs-you\";  // replaces its predecessor; never stacks\n\n/* Who actually needs a human — the same verdict the Alerts view and the beacon\n   read, so the notification can never disagree with the board it came from. */\n\nexport const NOTIFY_NAME_LIMIT = 3;\n\nexport function notificationsSupported() {\n  return typeof Notification !== \"undefined\";\n}\n\nexport function loadNotifyPreference() {\n  try {\n    state.notify.enabled = localStorage.getItem(NOTIFY_STORAGE_KEY) === \"on\";\n  } catch { state.notify.enabled = false; }\n  if (notificationsSupported()) state.notify.permission = Notification.permission;\n  // Permission revoked in browser settings between sessions: the stored\n  // preference is stale, so do not carry a promise we cannot keep.\n  if (state.notify.enabled && state.notify.permission !== \"granted\") state.notify.enabled = false;\n}\n\nexport function saveNotifyPreference() {\n  try { localStorage.setItem(NOTIFY_STORAGE_KEY, state.notify.enabled ? \"on\" : \"off\"); }\n  catch { /* storage unavailable */ }\n}\n\n/* The ONLY place permission is requested, and it is reachable only from a click.\n   Never on load: an unprompted permission dialog is how a page gets denied\n   permanently, which would silently disable the feature forever. */\n\n/* S1-T5. This read `alerting()` — the board's broad \"not healthy and not\n   finished\" verdict — which is a strict superset of \"a person is the blocker\".\n   The consequence was narrow and bad: the OS notification fired for a stalled\n   advisory while the button correctly stayed amber, so the one contract this\n   surface rests on (\"ember only when a person is the blocker\") broke at the\n   exact moment the operator is not looking at the screen to check it.\n\n   Repointed at the blocking half of the attention partition. This changes WHO\n   delivery fires for and nothing else — permission is still requested from a\n   click and never on load, NOTIFY_TAG still replaces rather than stacks, the\n   title still counts, and notificationPlan still only speaks about agents that\n   are NEW to the set. Targeting, not mechanics. */\nexport function needsHumanIds(snap) {\n  return blockingAgentIds(snap);\n}\n\n/* Pure. `prev === null` means \"we have not looked yet\": seed the baseline and\n   stay silent, which is what stops a reload from announcing the whole backlog. */\n\nexport function notificationPlan(prev, next, nameFor = null) {\n  const ids = next.slice().sort();\n  if (prev === null || prev === undefined) return { fire: false, ids, reason: \"seeded\" };\n  const before = new Set(prev);\n  const fresh = ids.filter((id) => !before.has(id));\n  if (!fresh.length) return { fire: false, ids, reason: \"no new agent needs you\" };\n  const names = fresh.slice(0, NOTIFY_NAME_LIMIT).map((id) => (nameFor && nameFor(id)) || id);\n  const rest = fresh.length - names.length;\n  return {\n    fire: true,\n    ids,\n    reason: \"new\",\n    title: fresh.length === 1 ? \"1 agent needs you\" : fresh.length + \" agents need you\",\n    body: names.join(\", \") + (rest > 0 ? \" and \" + rest + \" more\" : \"\"),\n  };\n}\n\n/* The zero-permission escalation: a background tab shows its own alert count. */\n\nexport function titleWithAlerts(base, count) {\n  const clean = String(base).replace(/^\\(\\d+\\)\\s*/, \"\");\n  return count > 0 ? \"(\" + count + \") \" + clean : clean;\n}\n\n/* \"Notifications\", never \"Alerts\". This control governs browser notification\n   delivery; the tab now called \"Needs you\" counts agents waiting on a human.\n   They were both labelled \"Alerts\" on adjacent surfaces with no shared meaning,\n   so \"Alerts off\" sat inches from \"Alerts 0\" and an operator could reasonably\n   read the first as an explanation of the second. */\nexport function notifyToggleView(notify, supported = notificationsSupported(), count = 0, tone = \"clear\") {\n  const n = Number.isFinite(count) && count > 0 ? count : 0;\n  const suffix = n ? ` · ${n} waiting on you` : \"\";\n  /* `tone` is the verdict, not a restatement of the count.\n     `blocked` means a PERSON is the blocker; `noticed` means the watcher has\n     something and nobody is waiting on you; `clear` means neither. It rides here\n     rather than being re-derived at the button because the badge's ink and the\n     panel's ember rail have to be the same judgement — a red button over a panel\n     with nothing red in it is the exact disagreement this surface replaced. */\n  const badgeTone = tone === \"blocked\" || tone === \"noticed\" ? tone : \"clear\";\n  const view = !supported\n    ? { label: \"Notifications unsupported\", pressed: false, disabled: true, title: \"This browser has no Notification API.\" }\n    : notify.permission === \"denied\"\n      ? { label: \"Notifications blocked\", pressed: false, disabled: true, title: \"Notifications are blocked for this site in your browser settings.\" }\n      : notify.enabled\n        ? { label: \"Notifications on\", pressed: true, disabled: false, title: \"Stop notifying me when an agent starts waiting.\" }\n        : { label: \"Notifications off\", pressed: false, disabled: false, title: \"Notify me when an agent starts waiting, even in another window.\" };\n  return {\n    ...view,\n    count: n,\n    tone: badgeTone,\n    title: view.title + suffix,\n    // The button's accessible name carries the backlog too — a screen reader\n    // must not have to infer it from a bare digit beside the label.\n    ariaLabel: view.label + (n ? `, ${n} agent${n === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"} waiting on you` : \"\"),\n    /* The DISCLOSURE's name, which is a different control from the delivery\n       switch above it.\n       The words above govern whether the browser may interrupt you; these\n       describe what is waiting inside the panel. They were one control until\n       the notification center existed, which is why \"Notifications off\" once\n       sat inches from four stopped agents and read as an explanation of them.\n       The badge's digit never stands alone here: \"1\" beside a red dot is not a\n       reading a screen reader can pass on. */\n    disclosureLabel: \"Notifications, \" + (\n      badgeTone === \"blocked\"\n        ? `${n} agent${n === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"} waiting on you`\n        : badgeTone === \"noticed\"\n          ? `${n} being watched, nobody waiting on you`\n          : \"nothing waiting\"\n    ),\n  };\n}\n\nexport function deliverNotification(plan, notify, ctor) {\n  if (!plan.fire) return plan.reason;\n  if (!notify.enabled) return \"muted\";\n  if (!ctor) return \"unsupported\";\n  if (notify.permission !== \"granted\") return \"not-granted\";\n  try {\n    // eslint-disable-next-line no-new\n    new ctor(plan.title, { body: plan.body, tag: NOTIFY_TAG });\n    return \"sent\";\n  } catch { return \"refused\"; }\n}\n\n/* Called on every adopted snapshot. The title always updates — it costs no\n   permission and cannot annoy anyone. The Notification only fires when the plan\n   says a NEW agent needs a human AND the operator opted in; denied, unsupported\n   or muted all degrade to the title alone, silently. */\n\nexport function applyNotifications(snap = state.snap) {\n  const next = needsHumanIds(snap);\n  const byId = agentsById(snap);\n  const plan = notificationPlan(state.notify.seen, next, (id) => {\n    const found = byId.get(id);\n    return found ? agentName(found.agent) : null;\n  });\n  state.notify.seen = plan.ids;\n  if (typeof document !== \"undefined\") {\n    document.title = titleWithAlerts(state.notify.baseTitle || document.title, next.length);\n  }\n  return deliverNotification(plan, state.notify, notificationsSupported() ? Notification : null);\n}\n\nexport async function toggleNotifications() {\n  if (state.notify.enabled) {\n    state.notify.enabled = false;\n    saveNotifyPreference();\n    renderNotifyToggle();\n    return;\n  }\n  if (!notificationsSupported()) { renderNotifyToggle(); return; }\n  let permission = Notification.permission;\n  if (permission === \"default\") {\n    try { permission = await Notification.requestPermission(); }\n    catch { permission = \"denied\"; }\n  }\n  state.notify.permission = permission;\n  state.notify.enabled = permission === \"granted\";\n  saveNotifyPreference();\n  renderNotifyToggle();\n}\n\n/* Denied is not an error state to shout about — the operator said no. The\n   control just reads \"unavailable\" and nothing else changes. */\n/* `count` is how many agents are waiting on a human right now, and it rides on\n   EVERY branch — muted, blocked and unsupported included. \"Notifications off\" sitting\n   silently beside four waiting agents was the whole defect: the button reported\n   the delivery channel and never the backlog. Turning notifications off is a\n   choice about interruption, not a reason to stop showing the number. */\n\n/* `tone`/`count` are passed in rather than re-derived: the panel computes the\n   feed once per paint and the badge is a reading off that same list. Deriving\n   them twice is how a button comes to disagree with the panel it opens. The\n   defaults keep the zero-argument call in render() honest before the first\n   snapshot lands. */\nconst BADGE_TONE_CLASS = { blocked: \"is-blocked\", noticed: \"is-noticed\", clear: \"is-clear\" };\n\nexport function renderNotifyToggle(count = 0, tone = \"clear\", open = false) {\n  const btn = $(\"notify-toggle\");\n  if (!btn) return;\n  const view = notifyToggleView(state.notify, notificationsSupported(), count, tone);\n  /* The label is \"Notifications\" in every state. It names what the control\n     governs, and it is the same word in the panel's footer switch and in\n     Settings; the delivery state it used to carry now lives on the switch that\n     actually changes it. */\n  btn.textContent = \"Notifications\";\n  /* The badge ALWAYS renders, zero included — a zero is a reading, an absent\n     badge is an absence, and an operator cannot tell \"nothing is waiting\" from\n     \"this stopped working\" by looking at a gap. The count is its own node so it\n     can take the ember treatment without entering the button's text content. */\n  btn.append(el(\"span\", {\n    class: \"notify-badge \" + BADGE_TONE_CLASS[view.tone],\n    \"aria-hidden\": \"true\",\n    text: String(view.count),\n  }));\n  /* A disclosure, not a switch. It never carries aria-pressed: the thing that\n     is on or off is delivery, and delivery's control is inside the panel. */\n  btn.removeAttribute(\"aria-pressed\");\n  btn.setAttribute(\"aria-expanded\", open ? \"true\" : \"false\");\n  btn.setAttribute(\"aria-controls\", \"notifications-panel\");\n  btn.setAttribute(\"title\", \"What needs a person right now.\");\n  btn.setAttribute(\"aria-label\", view.disclosureLabel);\n  /* Never disabled. Denied or unsupported delivery is a fact about the browser's\n     interruption channel; the list of who is waiting has nothing to do with it,\n     and locking the operator out of it because they declined a permission would\n     be the worst possible reading of \"no\". */\n  btn.removeAttribute(\"disabled\");\n  btn.classList.toggle(\"is-open\", open);\n  btn.classList.toggle(\"is-alerting\", view.tone === \"blocked\");\n}\n\n/* Delivery, kept separate from the decision so every gate is assertable without\n   a browser. Each refusal returns its own reason rather than a shared silence,\n   because \"we chose not to\" and \"the browser refused\" are different facts. */\n\n/* Presentation — how a session is NAMED and DESCRIBED to a person.\n\n   One question, answered once: given an agent, a program or an issue, what do\n   we call it and what do we say about it. Display names and the alias overrides\n   that beat them, the label targets a rename writes to, terminal identity and\n   its breadcrumb, why identity was quarantined and which surfaces collided,\n   role and model-policy readings, the issue lifecycle vocabulary, elapsed-clock\n   datasets, and the derived issue list.\n\n   Naming is the thing this codebase has re-forked and regretted before — the\n   comments below carry those scars — so it lives in exactly one place that both\n   the board and the drawer import. That is the seam: nobody re-derives a name.\n\n   Reads `state` for the alias map and the context-display preference, which is\n   why client-state.js had to come out first. Builds no DOM and issues no\n   requests: it decides WHAT to say, never where it lands on screen.  */\n\nimport { fmtElapsed, providerLabel, PROVIDER_LABELS } from \"./text-formatters.js\";\nimport { alerting, deriveActivity, deriveControlState, deriveOutcome, isTerminal, livenessState, provenanceOf } from \"./agent-model.js\";\nimport { state } from \"./client-state.js\";\nimport { ROLE_ALIASES, ROLE_LABELS } from \"./client-catalogs.js\";\n\nexport { ROLE_ALIASES, ROLE_LABELS };\n\n/* Plain words for provider-native enums that used to render raw. */\nexport const PROVENANCE_LABELS = { observed: \"measured\", estimated: \"estimated\", unknown: \"unknown\" };\n\nexport const IDENTITY_TIER_LABELS = {\n  recorded: \"Recorded target\",\n  session: \"Session ID on a terminal\",\n  cwd: \"Working folder\",\n};\n\nexport const IDENTITY_OUTCOME_LABELS = {\n  matched: \"matched\",\n  quarantined: \"quarantined\",\n  ambiguous: \"ambiguous\",\n  \"no-match\": \"no match\",\n  skipped: \"skipped\",\n  rejected: \"rejected\",\n};\n/* Why routing refused, and what the operator can actually DO about it — one\n   entry per shape the resolver produces. Deliberately ID-free: the banner is\n   Operate chrome and the established rule (controlUnavailableText, and the test\n   that pins it) is that raw cmux/session identifiers belong only in Evidence.\n   The specific \"ttys082 has both of these open\" answer is one click away in the\n   routing-evidence block, not in the banner. */\n\nexport const IDENTITY_CAUSES = {\n  \"contested-terminal\": {\n    why: \"More than one session claims the same terminal, so there is no unambiguous target to type into.\",\n    next: \"End or close one of the sessions sharing that terminal — controls re-arm on the next scan, no restart needed.\",\n  },\n  \"shared-folder\": {\n    why: \"This session is not registered on any terminal, and more than one session shares its working folder — so matching by folder cannot pick one.\",\n    next: \"Give this session its own cmux pane, or end the other session running in that folder; the next scan then binds it.\",\n  },\n  missing: {\n    why: \"No cmux terminal reports this session, so there is nothing to route Focus or Send to.\",\n    next: \"Open it in a cmux pane (or start the agent from one) and the next scan binds it.\",\n  },\n};\n\n// Progress 0–100 per work state (normative). blocked keeps a mid value but\n// its ember tone (not the %) carries the alarm.\n/* One server enum, one operator vocabulary. Every surface that names an\n   investigation state reads from here: the plan chip, the queue button and its\n   note, the pulse row's work state, the drawer eyebrow and the drawer status\n   sentence. Before this table `completed` read \"Complete\" on the chip,\n   \"complete · verifying\" on the button, \"verifying\" in the pulse row,\n   \"Verifying\" in the drawer eyebrow and \"complete · waiting for fresh data\" in\n   the drawer status — four different words for one state, on one board.\n   `work` maps into WORK_STATE_VIEW, which stays the downstream row vocabulary. */\nexport const INVESTIGATION_STATE_VIEW = {\n  queued: {\n    work: \"queued\", label: \"Queued\", tone: \"cool\",\n    button: \"✓ Investigation queued\",\n    note: \"Queued and ready for explicit launch\",\n    status: \"queued and ready for explicit launch\",\n  },\n  running: {\n    work: \"investigating\", label: \"Running\", tone: \"warm\",\n    button: \"● Investigation running\",\n    note: \"Investigation running\",\n    status: \"running\",\n  },\n  completed: {\n    work: \"verifying\", label: \"Verifying\", tone: \"ok\",\n    button: \"✓ Investigation verifying\",\n    note: \"Investigation verifying · waiting for fresh data\",\n    status: \"verifying · waiting for fresh data\",\n  },\n  blocked: {\n    work: \"blocked\", label: \"Blocked\", tone: \"hot\",\n    button: \"! Investigation blocked\",\n    note: \"Investigation blocked · review result\",\n    status: \"blocked · review result\",\n  },\n};\n\n/* A log that shows only successes is worse than no log: it reads as proof the\n   instruction landed. Every outcome the contract can return gets its own word. */\nexport const ACTION_OUTCOME_VIEW = {\n  ok: { label: \"Delivered\", tone: \"ok\" },\n  failed: { label: \"Failed\", tone: \"err\" },\n  partial: { label: \"Partly delivered\", tone: \"warn\" },\n  staged: { label: \"Staged — not submitted\", tone: \"warn\" },\n};\n\nexport function actionOutcomeView(outcome) {\n  // An outcome the server adds later reads as the server's own word rather than\n  // as a confident wrong label — the same rule investigationView follows.\n  return ACTION_OUTCOME_VIEW[outcome] || { label: String(outcome || \"unknown\"), tone: \"warn\" };\n}\n\nexport const agentLabelEligible = (agent) => Boolean(agent && agent.id);\n\n/* Live cmux / terminal title for this session, when routing knows one. */\n\nexport const agentLabelTarget = (agent) => ({ kind: \"agent\", agentId: agent.id });\n/* Every live agent can take a presentation label. Prefer editing the linked\n   cmux workspace when present so Ant Hill names stay hunt-able in the wild. */\n\n/* Did the FLEET declare this name, or derive it? The run manifest is where an\n   orchestrator writes what a lane IS — `fe-states`, `be-live` — and that id is\n   what the operator types to address it, what every sibling lane calls it, and\n   what the lane signs its own DONE line with.\n\n   The distinction is load-bearing directly below, because cmux titles its own\n   panes. `surfaceTitle` is routinely a sentence cmux distilled from the\n   session's opening prompt and `workspaceTitle` is the workspace path; neither\n   is a human deciding what a session is called. Counting them as renames put\n   \"Unify lane fe-states and audit tags with TDD\" on the Needs-you strip for a\n   lane the API named `fe-states`, and a workspace path on a swarm child the API\n   named `be-live` — one session reading three ways across three surfaces. */\nexport function declaredIdentity(agent) {\n  return Boolean(agent && agent.identity && agent.identity.source === \"manifest\");\n}\n\n/* The name a HUMAN typed for this row, or \"\" when nobody did: a label entered\n   in Ant Hill, then one typed onto the cmux pane itself. Split out from\n   agentName so a caller can tell \"the operator named this\" from \"the fleet\n   named this\" without comparing strings — the row needs that distinction to\n   decide whether the server's disambiguator belongs beside the name. */\nexport function operatorName(agent) {\n  if (!agent) return \"\";\n  const agentLabel = state.aliases.get(presentationLabelKey(agentLabelTarget(agent)));\n  if (agentLabel) return agentLabel;\n  if (agent.target && agent.target.workspaceId) {\n    const workspaceLabel = state.aliases.get(presentationLabelKey(workspaceLabelTarget(agent.target.workspaceId)));\n    if (workspaceLabel) return workspaceLabel;\n  }\n  const terminal = terminalSourceName(agent);\n  /* A SURFACE rename is this pane's own name and belongs to the session even\n     when the pane's folder differs — an orchestrator parked in the home\n     directory while its work lives in a project is the normal shape, not an\n     anomaly. A WORKSPACE title is broader context, so it stays suppressed on\n     that mismatch: otherwise the same home-cwd orchestrator borrows the name of\n     whichever project it happens to sit beside. */\n  /* ...and a DECLARED name outranks both, because cmux wrote both of them. The\n     title is not lost: quietSourceLine still prints it as \"Terminal: …\", which\n     is how an operator finds the pane, and which went silent here only while\n     the name and the title were the same string. */\n  const renamed = typeof agent.surfaceTitle === \"string\" && agent.surfaceTitle.trim() !== \"\";\n  if (terminal && !declaredIdentity(agent) && (renamed || agent.target?.cwdRelation !== \"different\")) return terminal;\n  return \"\";\n}\n\nexport function agentName(agent) {\n  if (!agent) return \"\";\n  return operatorName(agent) || sourceAgentName(agent);\n}\n\n/* Presentation-only labels. Source identities stay stable; the label is a\n   display value the operator controls. */\n\nexport function collisionClaimText(claim) {\n  const who = (PROVIDER_LABELS[claim.provider] || claim.provider) + \" \" + shortSessionId(claim.sessionId);\n  if (!claim.pid) return who;\n  return who + \" (pid \" + claim.pid + (claim.command ? \", \" + conciseText(claim.command, 40) : \"\") + \")\";\n}\n\nexport function collisionLine(collision) {\n  const where = collision.tty || collision.surfaceId || \"this terminal\";\n  if (!collision.claims.length) return where + \" — no open agent session files observed.\";\n  if (collision.claims.length === 1) return where + \" — one session open: \" + collisionClaimText(collision.claims[0]);\n  return where + \" — \" + collision.claims.length + \" sessions claim it: \"\n    + collision.claims.map(collisionClaimText).join(\" · \");\n}\n\nexport function conciseText(value, limit = 88) {\n  let text = String(value || \"\").split(\"\\n\")[0].replace(/^(goal:|you are)\\s*/i, \"\").trim();\n  /* The snippet is the line the operator reads to decide whether to act, and\n     it was spending its budget on transport: `[PR #21](https://github…)`\n     burned half the line saying \"PR #21\", and a cmux workspace UUID carries\n     zero decision value. Links keep their words, http URLs shrink to\n     host/…/tail, other schemes to their scheme, long hex runs to an\n     ellipsis. The full text stays in the drawer. */\n  text = text\n    .replace(/\\[([^\\]]+)\\]\\([^)]*\\)/g, \"$1\")\n    .replace(/\\bhttps?:\\/\\/\\S+/gi, (url) => {\n      const m = /^https?:\\/\\/([^/\\s]+)(?:\\/(\\S*))?$/.exec(url.replace(/[.,;)\\]}'\"]+$/, \"\"));\n      if (!m) return url;\n      const tail = m[2] ? m[2].split(/[/?#]/).filter(Boolean).pop() : \"\";\n      return tail ? m[1] + \"/…/\" + tail : m[1];\n    })\n    .replace(/\\b[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\\/\\/\\S+/gi, (url) => url.split(\"://\")[0] + \"://…\")\n    .replace(/\\b[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\\b/gi, \"…\")\n    .replace(/\\b[0-9a-f]{32,}\\b/gi, \"…\")\n    .replace(/\\s{2,}/g, \" \");\n  if (text.length <= limit) return text;\n  const clipped = text.slice(0, limit - 1);\n  const boundary = clipped.lastIndexOf(\" \");\n  return clipped.slice(0, boundary > limit * 0.65 ? boundary : clipped.length).trimEnd() + \"…\";\n}\n\n/* Plain-language control explanation for the Operate chrome. Never echoes\n   capability reasons here — live reasons carry raw cmux/session IDs, which\n   belong only in Evidence. */\nexport function controlUnavailableText(controlState, agent = null) {\n  /* Archived and dead both arrive here as \"observed-only\". They are different\n     facts and the summary line must not flatten them into a routing complaint.\n     (quarantineBrief owns the long form; this is the short one the dock's\n     accessible text uses.) */\n  if (agent && isTerminal(agent)) {\n    const why = provenanceOf(agent);\n    if (why === \"operator-archive\") return \"Controls are off because you archived this session.\";\n    if (why === \"provider-exit\") return \"Controls are off because the source recorded a session exit.\";\n    if (why === \"aged-out\") return \"Controls are off because this session left the scan window; only its record is kept.\";\n    if (why === \"process-died\" || livenessState(agent) === \"died\") {\n      return \"Controls are off because this session's process is gone — there is nothing left to receive them.\";\n    }\n    if (why === \"process-absent\") {\n      return \"Controls are off because no running process claims this session — there is nothing left to receive them.\";\n    }\n  }\n  /* Three sentences, because a refusal an operator cannot act on reads as a\n     fault: what is off, why, and what turns it back on. Send is OFF here, not\n     broken, and saying so is what stops the retry. */\n  if (controlState === \"unproven\") {\n    /* One sentence. Rendered at real drawer width it ran three paragraphs that\n       each said the same thing — the summary named the cause, the risk and the\n       recovery, then `why` restated the cause and the risk, then `nextStep`\n       restated the recovery. Repeating information under different labels is\n       the noise this board exists to cut, and a long refusal is likelier to be\n       skipped than a short one. The summary now states the refusal, `why` owns\n       the mechanism, and `nextStep` owns the action. */\n    return \"Send and Interrupt are off: cmux cannot confirm which session is on this pane.\";\n  }\n  return controlState === \"quarantined\"\n    ? \"Controls are unavailable — this session's identity is ambiguous, so control routing is quarantined.\"\n    : \"Controls are unavailable — no safe cmux target is linked to this session.\";\n}\n\n/* Short folder/Home identity for when cmux titles are unavailable. */\nexport function cwdIdentityName(agent) {\n  if (!agent || typeof agent.cwd !== \"string\" || !agent.cwd.trim()) return \"\";\n  const normalized = agent.cwd.replace(/\\/+$/, \"\");\n  const parts = normalized.split(\"/\").filter(Boolean);\n  const provider = providerLabel(agent.provider);\n  if (parts.length <= 2 && (parts[0] === \"Users\" || parts[0] === \"home\")) {\n    return provider + \" · Home\";\n  }\n  const base = parts[parts.length - 1];\n  return base ? provider + \" · \" + base : provider + \" · Home\";\n}\n\nexport function elapsedDataset(agent, generatedAt) {\n  const live = deriveActivity(agent) !== \"ended\" && agent.elapsedMs != null && generatedAt;\n  return live\n    ? { elapsedBase: String(agent.elapsedMs), elapsedFrom: generatedAt }\n    : {};\n}\n\n/* The destination as a VISIBLE label, not a tooltip.\n\n   focusDestinationHint below is a `title` attribute — the weakest disclosure\n   surface there is. It never appears on keyboard focus or touch, and an\n   operator who moves the mouse to the button and clicks reads nothing. The\n   strong wording lives in the drawer banner, which requires having already\n   stopped to investigate.\n\n   That is backwards for the row it matters on. `unique-cwd` is matched by\n   folder among panes carrying no identity evidence, so Focus can walk an\n   operator to a stranger's terminal while the row still reads healthy — and\n   naming the destination is what this project chose INSTEAD of gating the\n   control, because looking is how an operator recovers once the write controls\n   are off. A name nobody sees is not an alternative to gating.\n\n   Only on unproven rows: on a `linked` row the destination is proven and a\n   suffix on every button would be noise that trains the eye to skip it. */\nexport function focusButtonLabel(agent, controlState) {\n  if (controlState !== \"unproven\") return \"Focus\";\n  const id = terminalIdentity(agent);\n  const name = id ? (id.paneFolder || id.title) : \"\";\n  return name ? \"Focus → \" + name : \"Focus\";\n}\n\nexport function focusDestinationHint(agent) {\n  const id = terminalIdentity(agent);\n  if (!id) return \"Jump to terminal pane\";\n  const dest = [id.title, id.paneCwd].filter(Boolean).join(\" · \");\n  return dest ? \"Jump to \" + dest : \"Jump to terminal pane\";\n}\n\n/* Rename target: workspace first (shared terminal identity), else the agent. */\n\nexport function identityCause(view) {\n  const refused = (tier) => view.steps.some((step) =>\n    step.tier === tier && (step.outcome === \"quarantined\" || step.outcome === \"ambiguous\"));\n  if (refused(\"session\")) return \"contested-terminal\";\n  if (refused(\"cwd\")) return \"shared-folder\";\n  return \"missing\";\n}\n\n/* The banner's whole story: what happened, why, and what to do about it.\n   Returns null when controls route normally. Pure. */\n\n/* Normalized, render-ready view of one agent's identity trace. Pure. */\nexport function identityTraceView(agent) {\n  const trace = (agent && agent.identityTrace) || null;\n  const target = (agent && agent.target) || {};\n  const rawSteps = trace && Array.isArray(trace.steps) ? trace.steps : [];\n  return {\n    resolution: (trace && trace.resolution) || target.resolution || \"missing\",\n    matchedTier: (trace && trace.matchedTier) || null,\n    reason: (trace && trace.reason) || null,\n    surfaceId: (trace && trace.surfaceId) || target.surfaceId || null,\n    bridge: (trace && trace.bindingBridge) || null,\n    steps: rawSteps.map((step) => ({\n      tier: step.tier,\n      tierLabel: IDENTITY_TIER_LABELS[step.tier] || step.tier,\n      outcome: step.outcome,\n      outcomeLabel: IDENTITY_OUTCOME_LABELS[step.outcome] || step.outcome,\n      detail: step.detail || \"\",\n    })),\n  };\n}\n\n/* Which of the three real refusal shapes this is. Read off the tier that\n   actually refused, not off the resolution alone: every quarantine resolves as\n   \"ambiguous\", but a terminal contested by two sessions and a folder shared by\n   two sessions need different instructions. (Measured against the live board:\n   9 quarantined sessions, all `ambiguous`, all refused at the cwd tier.) */\n\n/* A state the server adds later reads as its own word everywhere rather than\n   as a confident wrong label on one surface and a raw enum on the next. */\nexport function investigationView(stateKey) {\n  if (INVESTIGATION_STATE_VIEW[stateKey]) return INVESTIGATION_STATE_VIEW[stateKey];\n  const raw = String(stateKey || \"queued\");\n  return {\n    work: \"queued\", label: raw, tone: \"cool\",\n    button: \"Investigation \" + raw,\n    note: \"Investigation \" + raw,\n    status: raw,\n  };\n}\n\nexport function issueLifecycle(issue) {\n  return issue && issue.lifecycle && issue.lifecycle.state\n    ? issue.lifecycle\n    : { state: \"open\" };\n}\n\nexport function issueLifecycleNote(issue) {\n  const lifecycle = issueLifecycle(issue);\n  if (lifecycle.state === \"verifying\") {\n    return `Verifying since ${issueTimestamp(lifecycle.verificationStartedAt)} · waiting for a fresh source snapshot to clear the finding.`;\n  }\n  if (lifecycle.state === \"blocked\") {\n    return `Blocked${lifecycle.result ? ` · ${lifecycle.result}` : \" · external action is required.\"}`;\n  }\n  return \"\";\n}\n\nexport function issueTimestamp(iso) {\n  if (!iso || Number.isNaN(Date.parse(iso))) return \"unknown time\";\n  return new Date(iso).toLocaleString([], { month: \"short\", day: \"numeric\", hour: \"numeric\", minute: \"2-digit\" });\n}\n\nexport function issuesOf(snap) {\n  if (!snap) return [];\n  const issues = [];\n  const server = Array.isArray(snap.issues) ? snap.issues : null;\n  if (server) {\n    /* The server owns the findings the client cannot see — collector faults,\n       source degradation, ended-session policy drift. It ALSO ships kind:\"agent\"\n       findings derived from outcome alone, and those are dropped here.\n\n       Dropping them is the whole fix for the false all-clear. Returning\n       snap.issues verbatim short-circuited the derivation below, so the rail\n       counted the server's agent rule while the tab counted alerting() — and the\n       board rendered \"NEEDS YOU 1 finding\", \"Needs you 0\" and \"Nothing needs\n       you\" at the same instant, each correct for its own hidden population.\n       Nothing is lost by dropping them: alerting() is a strict superset of the\n       server's rule (outcome not healthy AND not ended), and it additionally\n       catches the attentionSignal agents the server's rule misses entirely.\n\n       One collection, and its agent half is the tab's population by\n       construction rather than by coincidence. */\n    for (const issue of server) if (issue.kind !== \"agent\") issues.push(issue);\n  }\n  const errors = (!server && snap.controlHealth && snap.controlHealth.errors) || [];\n  if (errors.length) {\n    issues.push({\n      id: \"system:collector-errors\",\n      kind: \"system\",\n      severity: \"warning\",\n      title: \"Collection problems\",\n      summary: `${errors.length} collector problem${errors.length === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"} may make session data incomplete.`,\n      affectedAgentIds: [],\n      technicalDetails: [...errors],\n    });\n  }\n  for (const { agent } of snapshotAgents(snap)) {\n    const live = deriveActivity(agent) !== \"ended\";\n    const outcome = deriveOutcome(agent);\n    /* Bound to alerting(), the same verdict the tab, the notifier and the rollup\n       read, rather than re-deriving \"needs a human\" from outcome alone. That\n       third derivation is why an agent whose only claim was its attentionSignal\n       reached no surface at all. */\n    if (alerting(agent)) {\n      /* When the server said WHY, say that. Its evidence is the agent's own\n         words and its nextAction is the decision waiting — strictly better than\n         \"needs review\", which is the finding naming itself. */\n      const signal = agent.attentionSignal;\n      issues.push({\n        id: \"agent:\" + agent.id,\n        kind: \"agent\",\n        severity: outcome === \"failed\" ? \"error\" : \"warning\",\n        title: outcome === \"failed\" ? `${agentName(agent)} failed` : `${agentName(agent)} needs review`,\n        summary: (signal && signal.evidence) || agent.statusReason,\n        affectedAgentIds: [agent.id],\n      });\n    }\n    /* A per-session \"running a non-approved model\" finding was synthesized here,\n       one per mismatched Cursor session, on top of the server's single aggregate.\n\n       It was unreachable work twice over. The policy it enforced is gone (see\n       snapshot-agent.ts). And the row could never have been actioned even while\n       the policy stood: `policy:<agentId>` is an id the CLIENT invents, so it is\n       absent from snapshot.issues, and handleTriageRequest resolves triage\n       targets out of exactly that array — every Triage click on one of these\n       returned 404 ISSUE_NOT_FOUND. Seven such rows were on the live board.\n\n       The rule this leaves behind: this function may SHAPE what the server sent,\n       never mint an id the server has not published. Anything the client invents\n       has no counterpart to act on. */\n  }\n  return issues;\n}\n\n/* \"Did I already tell these lanes to rebase?\" — answered per agent, in the one\n   place where sending again is a click away. Newest-first is the contract, so\n   the first match is the most recent; sorting here would fight it. */\nexport function lastActionFor(actions, agentId) {\n  return (actions || []).find((a) => a.agentIds.includes(agentId)) || null;\n}\n\n/* Who it went to, without a wall of session ids. `nameFor` resolves what the\n   snapshot still knows; an agent that has since disappeared keeps its raw id\n   rather than being silently dropped from the record. */\n\n/* The SPAN reading as a NUMBER — first activity to last, dormancy included, with\n   the same live drift correction the cell applies so a running session's span\n   does not freeze between snapshots.\n\n   Split out of liveElapsedText because the Span lens buckets sessions by this\n   duration, and a lens that computed its own would be a second definition of\n   \"how long has this been going\" sitting one column away from the first. They\n   would agree until the day they did not, and the disagreement would show up as\n   a row that reads 9h sitting under a filter for \"1–8h\". One number, two\n   renderings. Returns null when the span is unmeasurable, which is a real state\n   and not a zero. */\nexport function liveElapsedMs(agent, generatedAt) {\n  if (agent.elapsedMs == null) return null;\n  if (deriveActivity(agent) !== \"ended\" && generatedAt) {\n    const drift = Date.now() - Date.parse(generatedAt);\n    if (Number.isFinite(drift) && drift > 0) return agent.elapsedMs + drift;\n  }\n  return agent.elapsedMs;\n}\n\nexport function liveElapsedText(agent, generatedAt) {\n  const ms = liveElapsedMs(agent, generatedAt);\n  return ms == null ? \"—\" : fmtElapsed(ms);\n}\n\n/* modelPolicyView() stood here, turning agent.modelPolicy into a compliance\n   badge. The field no longer exists — the hub judges no Cursor session on which\n   model it runs. The model itself is still collected and still rendered; only\n   the verdict about it is gone. */\n\nexport function preferredRenameTarget(agent) {\n  if (agent && agent.target && agent.target.workspaceId) {\n    return workspaceLabelTarget(agent.target.workspaceId);\n  }\n  return agentLabelTarget(agent);\n}\n\nexport function presentationLabelKey(target) {\n  if (!target) return \"\";\n  if (target.kind === \"program\") return \"program:\" + target.programId;\n  if (target.kind === \"workspace\") return \"workspace:\" + target.workspaceId;\n  if (target.kind === \"room\") return \"room:\" + target.surfaceId;\n  if (target.kind === \"agent\") return \"agent:\" + target.agentId;\n  return \"\";\n}\n\nexport const provenanceLabel = (p) => PROVENANCE_LABELS[p] || p || \"unknown\";\n\nexport function quarantineBrief(agent, control = deriveControlState(agent)) {\n  /* Three refusals now end in the same disabled button, and they are not the\n     same message. The pane one is recoverable by looking; the dead one is not\n     recoverable at all; the archived one is a choice the operator made. Both\n     `archived` and `died` collapse to the control state \"observed-only\", so\n     before this they shared one sentence about cmux routing — which is wrong\n     for both of them, and most wrong for archive, where nothing is broken.\n\n     Checked before the routing branches on purpose: an archived session's\n     controls are off because it is archived, whatever its pane says, and a dead\n     process cannot be typed into however cleanly it resolves. Naming the\n     routing problem of a session that has ENDED sends the operator to fix a\n     terminal binding that no longer matters. */\n  const ended = isTerminal(agent);\n  const why = provenanceOf(agent);\n  /* Four endings, four explanations. They all read \"You archived this session\"\n     before, including the ones no human had touched — so an operator was told\n     they had made a decision they had not made, about a session a provider\n     closed or that simply drifted out of the scan window. */\n  /* The contradiction, disclosed rather than resolved. An operator archive\n     outranks a live process — human intent wins — and a source can record an\n     exit while its harness lingers. Silently overturning either would be the\n     board deciding it knows better than the evidence in front of it; saying so\n     lets the operator decide. */\n  if (ended && livenessState(agent) === \"running\") {\n    return {\n      title: why === \"operator-archive\"\n        ? \"You archived this session, and its process is still running.\"\n        : \"This session ended, but its process is still up.\",\n      summary: why === \"operator-archive\"\n        ? \"Your decision stands — the board files it as finished — but something is still running under it.\"\n        : \"The source recorded a session exit while a matching process is still alive; the harness may be lingering.\",\n      why: \"These are two different sources of truth and they disagree. The board reports both rather than picking one quietly.\",\n      nextStep: why === \"operator-archive\"\n        ? \"Un-archive it if you filed it early, or leave it filed and let the process finish.\"\n        : \"Check the terminal if this is unexpected.\",\n      cause: \"archived\",\n      steps: [],\n    };\n  }\n  if (ended && why === \"provider-exit\") {\n    return {\n      title: \"This session ended.\",\n      summary: \"The source recorded a session exit, so there is nothing left to control.\",\n      why: \"A provider writes a session exit when the session itself closes — not when a turn finishes. Its transcript stays readable in History.\",\n      nextStep: \"Read it in History, or start a new session if there is more work.\",\n      cause: \"archived\",\n      steps: [],\n    };\n  }\n  if (ended && why === \"aged-out\") {\n    return {\n      title: \"This session left the scan window.\",\n      summary: \"Nothing ended it — the board simply stopped watching, and kept the record.\",\n      why: \"Collectors read transcripts inside the scan window. Past it a session is no longer observed, so no current evidence about it exists to control on.\",\n      nextStep: \"Widen the scan window in Settings if you need sessions this old back on the board.\",\n      cause: \"archived\",\n      steps: [],\n    };\n  }\n  /* Deliberately NOT branching on process-died here: the block below already\n     owns that sentence, and owns it better — it is the one refusal on this\n     board that offers no repair, because none exists. */\n  /* `process-absent` is excluded alongside `process-died` for the same reason\n     and one more: nobody archived these. They are the sessions the roster found\n     nothing running for, and telling an operator they filed it themselves is a\n     false claim about their own actions. */\n  if (ended && why !== \"process-died\" && why !== \"process-absent\") {\n    return {\n      title: \"You archived this session.\",\n      summary: \"Controls are off because it is archived, not because anything failed.\",\n      why: \"Archiving files a session as finished and takes it off the working board. It stays readable in History.\",\n      /* No repair step, because nothing is broken. Offering one would invent a\n         problem out of a deliberate choice. */\n      /* Finally true. This sentence shipped with the archive and had no store\n         method, endpoint or button behind it for its entire life. */\n      nextStep: \"Nothing to do. Un-archive it if you filed it early.\",\n      cause: \"archived\",\n      steps: [],\n    };\n  }\n  if (ended && (why === \"process-died\" || why === \"process-absent\" || livenessState(agent) === \"died\")) {\n    return {\n      title: \"This session's process is gone.\",\n      summary: \"Controls are off because there is nothing left running to receive them.\",\n      /* Two different observations reach this sentence and it says which. The\n         board watched one set of pids disappear; for the other it never saw a\n         process at all and is arguing from a complete scan of the machine. Both\n         mean the same thing for controls; only one is a death it witnessed. */\n      why: (why === \"process-absent\"\n        ? \"Every running process was listed and none of them is serving this session, so its terminal pane may since have been taken by something else.\"\n        : \"The process was checked and is no longer there, so its terminal pane may since have been taken by something else.\")\n        + \" Typing into it would reach whatever is there now.\",\n      /* Deliberately offers no recovery, because there is none. Every other\n         refusal on this board ends with the thing that would fix it, and\n         inventing one here would send an operator to retry something that\n         cannot work — the exact failure the whole refusal vocabulary exists to\n         prevent. */\n      nextStep: \"Nothing will bring it back. Read the transcript below, then archive it when you are done with it.\",\n      cause: \"died\",\n      steps: [],\n    };\n  }\n  if (control === \"linked\") return null;\n  const view = identityTraceView(agent);\n  const cause = identityCause(view);\n  /* Without this branch the banner throws. It renders whenever a write control\n     is disabled, and the fail-closed gate disables Send on a routable pane —\n     a state that previously could not exist, so this returned null and the\n     caller read .title off it. */\n  if (control === \"unproven\") {\n    const id = terminalIdentity(agent);\n    const focusTarget = id ? [id.title, id.paneCwd].filter(Boolean).join(\" · \") : \"\";\n    return {\n      title: \"Send is off for this row.\",\n      summary: controlUnavailableText(control),\n      why: \"It was matched by working directory alone, and a pane that changes directory into\"\n        + \" another's folder matches just as well — which is how an instruction reaches the wrong agent.\",\n      /* Focus NAMES its destination here, because on exactly these rows the\n         routing may be wrong. The adversarial verification found that a rotated\n         row keeps focus:true while its target has moved, so Focus can walk an\n         operator to a stranger's terminal. It stays enabled on purpose — it\n         types nothing, and going to look is how you recover when Send is off —\n         but \"go and look\" is only safe advice if the operator can tell, before\n         clicking, whether they arrived where they expected. The pane name was\n         already computed for a title attribute, which is to say it was visible\n         only on hover, which is to say it was not visible. */\n      nextStep: focusTarget\n        ? `Focus still works and will take you to ${focusTarget} — check that is the session you meant.`\n          + \" Nothing here needs repairing: Send returns on its own once cmux names the session.\"\n        : \"Focus still works, so open the pane and look. Nothing here needs repairing:\"\n          + \" Send returns on its own once cmux names the session.\",\n      cause,\n      steps: view.steps,\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    title: control === \"quarantined\" ? \"Control routing locked.\" : \"Controls unavailable.\",\n    summary: controlUnavailableText(control),\n    why: IDENTITY_CAUSES[cause].why,\n    nextStep: IDENTITY_CAUSES[cause].next,\n    cause,\n    steps: view.steps,\n  };\n}\n\n/* Short form of a provider session id — long enough to tell two sessions on\n   one terminal apart, short enough to read in a sentence. */\n\nexport function recentlyResolvedOf(snap) {\n  return snap && Array.isArray(snap.recentlyResolved) ? snap.recentlyResolved : [];\n}\n\n/* ---------- message provenance ----------\n\n   The producer helper prefixes every orchestrator→lane message with\n   `[from <agent.id> run <runId>]`. That envelope is the answer to a question the\n   drawer was getting wrong: `lastUserMessage` is labelled \"You\", and for every\n   lane in every swarm it was sent by another AGENT, not by the operator.\n\n   Anchored at the START, deliberately. An agent quoting an instruction back\n   before answering is extremely common — this file already carries a scar from\n   a dedup rule that mistook a quote for a repeat — and a header in the middle of\n   prose is a session TALKING about a message, not a claim about who sent this\n   one. Provenance is only a fact when it is the envelope.\n\n   The absence of a header is itself the signal: a user turn with none really was\n   the human, which is what makes an injected instruction distinguishable. */\nconst SENDER_HEADER = /^\\s*\\[from\\s+([^\\s\\]]+)\\s+run\\s+([^\\s\\]]+)\\]\\s*/;\n\nexport function parseSenderHeader(text) {\n  const value = typeof text === \"string\" ? text : \"\";\n  const match = SENDER_HEADER.exec(value);\n  if (!match) return null;\n  const [envelope, agentId, runId] = match;\n  if (!agentId || !runId) return null;\n  return { agentId, runId, body: value.slice(envelope.length).trim() };\n}\n\n/* Which fields actually carry it, measured rather than assumed: on the live\n   board the envelope sits on `lastUserMessage` and `task`, and on NEITHER of the\n   four atlas lanes' `lastHumanMessage` — that field mirrored the agent's own\n   reply. It is left out on purpose as well as on evidence: filling an\n   attribution from the one field the server documents as \"assistant OR user\n   prose\" is precisely how the \"You\" mislabel got in. */\n/* WHICH field the sender claim is read from — the mirror of `senderClaimFor` in\n   src/server/sender-verification.ts, and it has to stay a mirror, because the\n   server verifies the claim it reads and the client attributes the claim it\n   reads. Two different answers means the board says \"confirmed\" about a message\n   nobody checked.\n\n   A present `lastUserMessage` IS the current request and is authoritative even\n   with no header: an unheaded user turn really was the human, and that absence\n   is the whole signal that makes an injected instruction visible. `task` is only\n   the fallback, because it stays headed forever — the kickoff envelope is still\n   sitting on it hours later. Falling through to it attributed a human's own\n   follow-up to the orchestrator that opened the lane, on a row whose current\n   request had no sender at all. */\nexport function senderClaimText(agent) {\n  if (!agent) return undefined;\n  return typeof agent.lastUserMessage === \"string\" ? agent.lastUserMessage : agent.task;\n}\n\nexport function senderOf(agent) {\n  const parsed = parseSenderHeader(senderClaimText(agent));\n  return parsed ? { agentId: parsed.agentId, runId: parsed.runId } : null;\n}\n\n/* The prose without its addressing. A row gets ~120 characters and the envelope\n   is 74 of them, so this is not tidiness — it is half the line back. */\nexport function withoutSenderHeader(text) {\n  const parsed = parseSenderHeader(text);\n  if (parsed) return parsed.body;\n  return typeof text === \"string\" ? text : \"\";\n}\n\n/* How a role was decided, as something an operator can SEE. 1006 sessions on\n   the live board carry `inferred` against 4 `declared`, so a role chip that\n   renders a guess and a declaration identically is stating false confidence\n   about almost the whole fleet. Whole class-name literals: styles.css's orphan\n   lint reads the source as text and a name built at runtime is invisible to it\n   in both directions. */\nexport const ROLE_SOURCE_VIEW = {\n  declared: {\n    className: \"role-src-declared\",\n    title: \"Role declared at spawn — from the run manifest or ANTHILL_ROLE\",\n  },\n  observed: {\n    className: \"role-src-observed\",\n    title: \"Role observed from lineage — this session has children of its own\",\n  },\n  inferred: {\n    className: \"role-src-inferred\",\n    title: \"Role inferred from the session title — a guess, not a declaration\",\n  },\n};\n\nexport function roleSourceView(roleSource) {\n  return ROLE_SOURCE_VIEW[roleSource] || null;\n}\n\n/* Territory, not authority — which is why B4 took frontend/backend out of the\n   role union. It still has to reach the screen: before the demotion those\n   sessions read \"Frontend / designer\", and after it they read \"Worker\" with the\n   fact on the wire and nowhere else. */\nexport const SPECIALTY_LABELS = { frontend: \"Frontend\", backend: \"Backend\" };\n\nexport function specialtyLabel(agent) {\n  return (agent && SPECIALTY_LABELS[agent.specialty]) || \"\";\n}\n\nexport function roleView(role) {\n  const normalized = String(role || \"agent\")\n    .trim()\n    .toLowerCase()\n    .replace(/[-_]+/g, \" \")\n    .replace(/\\s*\\/\\s*/g, \" / \")\n    .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \");\n  const key = ROLE_ALIASES[normalized] || ROLE_LABELS[normalized] ? normalized : \"agent\";\n  const canonical = ROLE_ALIASES[key] || (ROLE_LABELS[key] ? key : \"agent\");\n  return { key: canonical, label: ROLE_LABELS[canonical] };\n}\n\n/* Header \"Typical request\": prefer the server-computed median; otherwise a\n   narrow fallback — the median of live latest-invocation totals we can see. */\n\nexport const roomLabelTarget = (surfaceId) => ({ kind: \"room\", surfaceId });\n\nexport function shortSessionId(id) {\n  const text = String(id || \"\");\n  return text.length > 10 ? text.slice(0, 8) + \"…\" : text;\n}\n\n/* GET /api/debug/identity?agent=<id> → the sentence the operator needs: which\n   terminal, and which sessions are fighting over it. The pids/commands/open\n   files live only on CmuxSurface, which the snapshot does not carry, so this is\n   the one piece of evidence that has to be fetched on demand. Pure. */\n\nexport function snapshotAgents(snap) {\n  if (!snap) return [];\n  return snap.programs.flatMap((p) => p.agents.map((agent) => ({ agent, program: p })));\n}\n\nexport function sourceAgentName(agent) {\n  if (!agent) return \"\";\n  /* The server decided this, across the whole fleet, and it is the only answer\n     that can be unique.
